correctness.rationale: For each lag j=t-k-1 the exact probability lies between (1-q)q^j and q^j. Independent Bernoulli choices yield the uniform log moment bound m[s²/(2β)+Oβ(s+1)] by splitting the geometric product at j=floor(s/β). At s=βr/m this gives log upper tail at most −βr²/(2m)+O(r+1). Requiring all m hits at the first h=ceil(r/m) arrivals costs at most βmh(h−1)/2−mh log(1−q) in negative log probability, with the same leading coefficient. Taking disjoint birth intervals gives order n/(h+1) independent witnesses, without assuming independent degrees. The upper union bound and lower no-witness probability are summable at n=2^j at the respective (1±ε) thresholds. Monotonicity and consecutive dyadic log ratios extend the simultaneous rational-ε bounds to all n; the root convention and a uniform additive m compare the two maxima. This verifies the almost-sure limit for fixed m and β and with multiplicity only. The inspected artifacts/verify.py is a replay of finite rational identities, not the limit proof, and was not executed.
